en.title: Counting Three-Character Subsequences
en.description:
Count how many times a pattern string of length exactly 3 occurs in the text as a subsequence. Occurrences are distinguished by the triple of kept positions; they need not be contiguous, and repeated letters are still counted by position.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line is the pattern, and the second line is the text. The pattern has length 3 and the text has length 1..500000; both contain only A..Z.
en.output: Output the exact integer, without taking a modulus, using a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: The three examples have 5, 4, and 0 choices of positions, respectively.
hints: Maintain, updating in reverse order, the number of ways to match the first 0, 1, 2, 3 characters of the pattern; initially dp[0]=1.
